name: Hull
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Hull, MA 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Hull, MA: the Lobster Trap Tree Lighting with Santa on a fire truck, Flying Santa and the Festival of Trees at the Lifesaving Museum.
lede: Hull celebrates Christmas the way a beach town should, with a tree made of lobster traps at Mariner's Park, Santa landing by helicopter at the old lifesaving station and a boathouse full of decorated trees.
celebrates: Christmas in Hull happens along Nantasket Avenue and the harbor. The Nantasket Beach Saltwater Club lights a Lobster Trap Tree at the Mariner's Park gazebo, where Santa arrives by fire truck and the club serves cocoa, cider and cookies. At the Hull Lifesaving Museum, Flying Santa lands for a quick visit with children as one of his Candy Cane Stops, and the museum's Festival of Trees fills its Windmill Point Boathouse with trees decorated by local businesses and families, later donated to veterans. The museum also hosts a Christmas Bird Count, a tradition that dates back to 1901.
lastyear: In 2025 the Hull Lifesaving Museum held its Festival of Trees at the museum on Nantasket Avenue, with more than 20 decorated Christmas trees on display through December 20, 2025. Down the street, the Paragon Carousel held its annual pictures with Santa on Saturday, December 6, 2025, from noon to 3 pm. For 2026 the museum moves the festival to its Windmill Point Boathouse on Main Street, with more than 30 trees.
facts: The Hull Lifesaving Museum sits in the Point Allerton US Lifesaving Station, built in 1889 and home to Captain Joshua James and his crews, whom the museum calls the most celebrated lifesavers in the world. The museum's prized boat is the surfboat Nantasket. Flying Santa, who now lands there, began in 1929 by dropping gifts to lighthouse keepers from a floatplane. The Paragon Carousel on Nantasket Avenue finished its 98th season in October 2026.
trains: Hull has no train station of its own. The closest MBTA Commuter Rail stop is Nantasket Junction on the Greenbush Line, at 190 Summer Street in Hingham, with trains to South Station in Boston. The MBTA's Hingham/Hull Ferry also stops at Hull (Pemberton Point) on the way to Long Wharf, so check its current schedule. For a holiday train ride, Edaville in Carver runs a train through its Christmas lights, and the Boston Street Railway Association shares streetcar history.

faq: What is the Hull Lobster Trap Tree?

It is a Christmas tree made of lobster traps, lit each December at the Mariner's Park gazebo at 3 Fitzpatrick Way. The Nantasket Beach Saltwater Club hosts the lighting as a free community event, with Santa arriving by fire truck, photos with the Little Red Truck, and cocoa, cider and cookies for everyone.
What is Flying Santa in Hull?

Flying Santa is a New England tradition that began in 1929, when Santa dropped gifts to lighthouse keepers from a floatplane. Today he visits Coast Guard stations by helicopter, and the Hull Lifesaving Museum is one of his Candy Cane Stops, where children can greet him during a quick landing and take a photo.
Where is the Hull Festival of Trees?

The Hull Lifesaving Museum runs its Festival of Trees at the Windmill Point Boathouse, 185 Main Street. Local businesses and families sponsor and decorate the trees, visitors vote for a favorite, and after the festival the trees are donated to veterans and their loved ones. The museum charges a single or family admission.
How do you get to Hull without a car?

Hull has no Commuter Rail station. The nearest stop is Nantasket Junction on the Greenbush Line in Hingham, at 190 Summer Street. The MBTA's Hingham/Hull Ferry also stops at Hull (Pemberton Point) on trips to and from Long Wharf in Boston, so families can check the ferry schedule for a boat ride into the city.
